For fixed, L2-normalized item TF–IDF vectors, cosine similarity is a dot product ([documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer.html)). Derived implementation: compute masked similarities S[j,k] once; maintain A[t,j]=A[t−1,j]+S[j,t]. Each prefix updates O(L) sums, so all recurrence weights cost O(L²), excluding feature dimension. Combine A[t,j] with recency, mask j>t, normalize over valid positions, then pool embeddings. Prefix-dependent TF–IDF refitting invalidates this recurrence because previous similarities change.

Zero padding rows/columns explicitly; return zero for empty prefixes and define zero-vector cosine safely. If excluding self-similarity, subtract the actual diagonal, preserving distinct occurrences of repeated items unless deduplication is explicitly intended. Sliding windows require subtracting departing similarities. Truncated-history equivalence requires identical retained events, recency coordinates, normalization and position indexing; full-history sums cannot substitute for truncated sums. SASRec’s learned positions and final-position scoring make these details consequential ([original implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py)).

Calibrate the pooled residual against SASRec feature norms, with epsilon protection and documented gradient handling. For g=σ(b), dg/db=g(1−g): near-zero gates suppress gate and branch learning, potentially hiding a useful residual. A small external residual scale with a nonsaturated gate, or a directly learned zero-initialized scalar, merits comparison; the latter follows [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887). Assessment: substantial implementation difficulty, including numerical behavior and predictor parity. Verify optimized versus brute-force prefixes, padding, repeats, empty metadata and truncated windows; compare exported predictor scores using identical checkpoints, metadata transforms, routing, masks and evaluation mode. No evidence here establishes recommendation gains.
